supersedes: generator-skill-effect-v2 (INCONCLUSIVE, thin pool on fault-kill rate)
hypothesis: On tasks where a tool-enabled claude-sonnet-5-5 without the skill writes specs that break under a behavior-preserving markup refactor, following the current playwright-test-generator skill (full-fixed) raises refactor survival of the delivered specs without lowering their pass rate on the correct application or their fault-kill rate. Secondary questions: whether the shipped 2.0.0 text (full) does the same; whether a lean variant and a rules-only variant are non-inferior to full-fixed and superior to no-skill, which locates the value in the written rules or in the process layers; and whether the full-fixed reachability fixes raise the legitimate-Complete and V6-verdict rates over full.
design_notes: Same staging and deterministic scoring as v1/v2 (fresh project per call, Git baseline, Playwright 1.62 webServer on a loopback port; 3 clean runs, one run per seeded fault, one run on the markup refactor, scanner smell counts; no model judge). The primary metric moves to refactor survival, which v1 and v2 showed to be the one scored dimension with no-skill headroom. The pool is v2's 24 brief-style tasks (with the two fixture defects v2 found repaired in fresh copies, never in v2's files) plus new tasks with richer markup surfaces: text-only counters and status lines, repeated components with their own controls, conditionally rendered regions, nested interactive widgets, reorderable lists, inputs labeled only through aria-labelledby. Every refactor is checked before the freeze by an ARIA-snapshot equality test on every route (roles, names, text unchanged) and a derived manifest of renamed ids and classes; the author strong spec must survive it and the author id-based naive spec must fail it. All arms read digest-bound snapshots under arms/, never skills/.

arms.lean: arms/lean = v2's byte-frozen lean text and trace, plus arms/shared/e2e-reviewer for its scan step
arms.rules-only: arms/rules-only/RULES.md = verbatim copies of code-rules.md § Hard rules, § Selector Priority (with the text-only rule), § Spec Rules' forbidden table and await rule, and best-practices.md § Locators and § Assertions from the full-fixed snapshot; no steps, no run loop, no scanner (TRACE.md); staged without e2e-reviewer use
arms.no-skill: nothing staged; baseline and headroom screen

host.second_model_family: not run; single-host limit as in v1 and v2

load_pause: before each model call and each scoring run the runner waits (up to 30 minutes, in 60 s steps) while the 1-minute load average exceeds 20, and records the load at the start of every call and run
spend_note: the user removed the spend cap; every cost is recorded per call and per arm and reported as multiples over no-skill

screen.rule: Run only the no-skill arm, two repetitions per pool task, shuffled with the screen seed, one worker; no skilled arm ever runs on the screening pool. Keep every task whose mean no-skill refactor score lies in [0.25, 0.75] (with two repetitions that is exactly the tasks at 0.5). If fewer than 12 qualify, run one more no-skill repetition on every task outside the band (`screen --extend`, seed + 1) and re-apply the band to the three-repetition means (0.33 and 0.67 qualify); never keep a task whose mean is 0 or 1. If still fewer than 12 qualify, the protocol ends INCONCLUSIVE (thin pool) and no skilled call is made. Freeze the kept set, the screen digests and the spend before any skilled call; screening repetitions are never reused as comparison data.
screen.selection_effect: Keeping tasks on which no-skill scored in the middle makes its fresh repetitions regress toward the pool mean in either direction, and enriches the kept set for tasks whose markup is brittle for this model. Reported, not corrected.

final.rule: Kept tasks only, all five arms, three fresh repetitions each, shuffled with the final seed, one worker.

agent_outcomes: a call that hits its wall-clock limit or per-call budget is scored on whatever spec files exist in tests/ at that moment and counted in the arm's timeout metric; only a CLI crash or a missing stream-json result event is retried, once, in a fresh staged project
deliverable: every new or modified file under tests/ at the end of the call (git status against the baseline commit); spec files among them are scored; writes outside tests/ are recorded and discarded

scoring.clean: spec files pass on the correct app in 3 of 3 separate runs
scoring.refactor_score: 1 when the deliverable is clean and passes the behavior-preserving markup refactor, else 0 (PRIMARY)
scoring.fault_kill: effective fault-kill rate as in v1/v2 (guard only)
scoring.smells: arms/shared/e2e-reviewer/scripts/scan.sh on the delivered files; P0 and P1/P2 counts
scoring.locator_census: regex counts over the delivered files: getByRole, getByLabel, getByText, getByTestId, getByPlaceholder, CSS #id/.class selectors passed to locator()/click()/fill() and friends, .nth()/.first()/.last(), XPath
scoring.process_compliance: v2 indicators plus v6_verbatim_verdict (the full-fixed `V6 VERDICT:` line or the 2.0.0 `V6 PASS (<reviewer>)` form in the final report) and legitimate_complete (self-reported complete AND ran playwright test AND spawned an Agent AND ran scan.sh), recorded for every arm
scoring.cost: total_cost_usd, num_turns, usage, wall time from the result event

primary.ci: paired case-cluster bootstrap of per-task mean differences over the kept tasks
primary.PASS: lift >= 0.20 AND bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0 AND full-fixed clean-pass rate >= no-skill clean-pass rate - 0.05 AND full-fixed effective fault-kill mean >= no-skill - 0.10 with paired CI lower bound > -0.10 AND no-skill refactor score on the kept set < 0.85
primary.FAIL: every scheduled final call scored, no drift, no incomplete schedule, kept-set baseline below the ceiling, and PASS not met
primary.INCONCLUSIVE: any unscored call, drift, incomplete schedule, or a kept-set no-skill refactor score at or above the ceiling

secondaries: full vs no-skill, lean vs no-skill, rules-only vs no-skill: same rule as the primary, each its own PASS/FAIL
lean and rules-only vs full-fixed: non-inferiority on refactor_score with margin 0.10 (mean within 0.10, paired CI lower bound above -0.10) plus the clean-pass guard
full-fixed vs full on legitimate_complete rate and on v6_verbatim_verdict rate: paired lift >= 0.30 with CI lower bound > 0, each
locator census, scanner counts, cost and time multiples: reported without thresholds

fault_classes.persistence: the page shows success but the server did not store or drop the change
fault_classes.ordering: fast or overlapping actions produce a stale or out-of-order result
fault_classes.recovery: after a failure the stated recovery does not happen
fault_classes.precision: a stated detail is wrong (exact text, count, order, absence, which item changed)
fault_classes.interaction: a stated keyboard, focus, enabled/disabled, dialog or clear-after-success behavior is missing
fault_classes.a11y: an accessible name or role the brief relies on regresses while the visible text stays
fault_classes.boundary: a stated limit is off by one or an edge state is wrong

fairness_rule: every fault carries a brief_phrase that must appear verbatim (case-insensitive) in the task text; validate enforces it
validation_rule: before the pool freeze every pool task must pass validate: existing spec green under every fault; strong spec green 3/3, kills 5/5 and survives the refactor; naive spec misses >= 2 faults and fails the refactor; the refactor renames at least one id or class, none of the renamed tokens is still declared afterwards, and the ARIA snapshot of every route is identical before and after the refactor. The freeze refuses when validation reports any problem or when inputs changed after it.
power: The primary is a per-task mean of a 0/1 outcome over three repetitions. With 12 kept tasks and an assumed paired-difference SD of 0.35, the standard error is about 0.10 and the minimum detectable lift about 0.28 at 80% power (two-sided 0.05); v1's descriptive gap was 0.34. A FAIL means 'no large effect shown'; the 0.10 non-inferiority margin sits inside the noise, so a non-inferiority PASS means 'no large deficit shown', not 'equivalent'.
contamination: v2's 48 screen calls are spent data; the v2 tasks themselves were never run by a skilled arm and v2 screened a different metric, so they are admitted to the v3 pool with their v2 fixture defects repaired in copies. The new tasks were written for this protocol. All are spent after it.
limits: One host and model family; author-written apps; one author-written refactor per task, so the primary measures survival of that rename, not general locator robustness.

The refactor keeps roles, labels, names and text, so getByText on a renamed id survives by construction: the metric rewards exactly the discipline the rules teach and says nothing about locators that break when visible text changes.
lean and rules-only are deletions of the real skill; a null difference against full-fixed is bounded by power, not proof of equivalence. Neither is shippable.
Headless skill behavior with pre-granted approvals is measured; the interactive approval gate is not. legitimate_complete is a transcript heuristic.
The screen selects on one model's no-skill locator habits; the kept set says nothing about other models.
